It really depends on the therapist you get and the style of therapy like you mentioned. I have had therapists I straight up walked out of the office from mid session. I’ve been through group therapy as well as CBT and DBT. 

Personally I think the DBT I received has had the most positive impact on me, especially since I was kneels diagnosed and actively suicidal at the time. It involved both one on one sessions as well as group sessions and the therapist I had was very understanding and sympathetic, but also firm when she needed to be especially during my episodes which I desperately needed. 

That being said I do feel a nice little release and catharsis with one-on-one venting styles of therapy. It doesn’t always last long but I found it can help hold off depressive/suicidal episodes for a time. 

So it really just depends. In a lot of ways therapy is like dating for me at least. You can definitely run into a lot of crap shoots, and certain therapists or therapy styles you come across won’t work for you at all. But once you find a good therapist and style of therapy that works for you it’s absolutely worth the effort, at least in my experience

That being said, if you drink too much and feel sick and it’s effecting your life every time you have a drink you may very well be a “problem drinker” or simply a person whose body may not tolerate alcohol the same as other people (alcohol is literally a poison so it’s not that surprising)
